outputs.exact_statement: For every $a,b\ge1$, there are a positive integer $n$ and an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ such that, with $L=[-1,1]^n$, $$\log N(K,L)>b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ).$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite nonempty sets, and let $g_y\colon X\to\mathbb R$, $y\in Y$, be real functions. Write $$R_x=(g_y(x))_{y\in Y}\in\mathbb R^Y,
 \qquad
 f_\lambda=\sum_{y\in Y}\lambda_y g_y,
 \qquad
 \mathcal F=\{f_\lambda:\|\lambda\|_1\le1\}.$$ Suppose that $$\|R_x-R_{x'}\|_\infty\ge1
 \quad\text{for all distinct }x,x'\in X,$$ and that, for some $\varepsilon>0$, there is a list of $M$ functions on $X$ such that every member of $\mathcal F$ is within $\varepsilon$ of a function on the list in the uniform norm. The functions on the list need not belong to $\mathcal F$. For $t>0$, set $$K=3\mathop{\mathrm{absconv}}\{R_x:x\in X\}+tB_\infty^Y,
 \qquad L=B_\infty^Y.$$ Then $K,L$ are origin-symmetric compact convex bodies with nonempty interior in $\mathbb R^Y$, and $$\label{eq:matrix-body-bounds}
 N(K,L)\ge |X|,
 \qquad
 N\bigl(L^\circ,(6\varepsilon+2t)K^\circ\bigr)\le M.$$ Both covering numbers use arbitrary ambient translation centers.

Under the hypotheses above, there is a finite list $\mathcal A$ of real-valued functions on $X$, of cardinality $Q$, such that every $f\in\mathcal F_+$ has an approximant $A\in\mathcal A$ satisfying $$f(x)-3\theta\le A(x)\le f(x)+\theta\qquad(x\in X).
  \label{eq:positive-approximation}$$ In particular, $\|f-A\|_{\infty,X}\le3\theta$. The list can be chosen with $$\log Q\le hs\log q+C_{h,\theta,u},
  \qquad
  C_{h,\theta,u}
   =\log u+hs2^u\log\left(1+\frac{s2^u}{\theta}\right).
  \label{eq:compression-count}$$

With the notation of Proposition 4, put $$f_\lambda=\sum_{y\in Y}\lambda_y g_y, \qquad B_1^Y=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^Y:\sum_{y\in Y}|\lambda_y|\le1\right\},$$ and $$\mathcal F=\{f_\lambda:\lambda\in B_1^Y\} =\mathop{\mathrm{absconv}}\{g_y:y\in Y\}.$$ There is a list of at most $Q^2$ functions which approximates every member of $\mathcal F$ to uniform error $6\theta$. Moreover, $B_1^Y$ can be partitioned into at most $Q^2$ nonempty clusters such that $$\|f_\lambda-f_{\lambda'}\|_{\infty,X}\le12\theta \label{eq:signed-cluster-diameter}$$ whenever $\lambda,\lambda'$ belong to the same cluster.

Let $P\in\mathbb F_p[z_1,\ldots,z_k]$ be a nonzero polynomial of total degree at most $d$, where $k,d$ are nonnegative integers and $p$ is prime. If $U_1,\ldots,U_k$ are independent and uniform in $\mathbb F_p$, then $$\Pr\bigl(P(U_1,\ldots,U_k)=0\bigr)\le \frac{d}{p}.$$

Let $0<\theta<1$ and let $r,h$ be positive integers. Put $$w=2D_h,\qquad
  u=\left\lceil\frac{hw}{\theta}\right\rceil,
  \label{eq:field-parameters}$$ and let $p$ be any prime satisfying $$p>\max\{h,h^2u^{2h}\}.
  \label{eq:field-prime-threshold}$$ There exist $t_1,\ldots,t_u\in E=\mathbb F_p^r$ such that, for every nonzero $Z\in\operatorname{Sym}^h(E^*)$, there is a set $T\subseteq[u]$ with $|[u]\setminus T|\le\theta u$ for which $$Z(t_{i_1},\ldots,t_{i_h})\ne0
  \qquad\text{for all }(i_1,\ldots,i_h)\in T^h.
  \label{eq:robust-nonvanishing}$$ Tuples in this assertion may have repeated indices.

With the parameters and directions of Proposition 7, let $$X=\operatorname{Sym}^h(E^*),\qquad L_i(x)=x(t_i,\cdot,\ldots,\cdot),$$ and let $\mathcal T=\{T\subseteq[u]:|[u]\setminus T|\le\theta u\}$. Then $|X|=m=p^{D_h}$, and each label map $L_i$ has at most $q=p^{D_{h-1}}$ realized labels. For the partition graphs of Section 3, every pair of distinct $x,y\in X$ has some $T\in\mathcal T$ satisfying $$d_T(x,y)>h. \label{eq:graph-separation}$$ Consequently, for $Y=X\times\mathcal T$ and $R_x=(g_{(v,T)}(x))_{(v,T)\in Y}\in\mathbb R^Y$, the rows satisfy $$\|R_x-R_y\|_\infty=1\qquad(x\ne y). \label{eq:row-separation}$$
For every $A,C\ge1$, there are an integer $n\ge1$ and an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ such that, with $L=[-1,1]^n$, $$\log N(K,L)>C\log\widehat M(K,L/A).$$

purpose: Counterexamples to the duality conjecture for metric entropy

coverage.checked_domain: All nonzero coefficient arrays of degrees at most 0 and 1 over primes 2 and 3; degree at most 3 over prime 2; degree at most 2 over primes 3 and 5. Trailing zero coefficients are included.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact symbolic polynomial evaluation over the prime field independently counts every field element. Integer root counts are compared to the actual polynomial degree; no sampling or solver witness is used.

title: Counterexamples to the duality conjecture for metric entropy

evidence.quote: On the finite-dimensional space $\mathcal F(N)$, the identity remains a finite-rank operator of norm at most one.

exclusions.query: Finite metric counterexample to bounded approximation
exclusions.reason: On the finite free space the identity itself has finite rank; the anchor obstruction uses an infinite block.

outputs.exact_statement: There is a countable, unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space $(M,d,o)$ such that $d(x,y)\ge1$ for distinct points and $\mathcal F(M)$ has AP but fails $\lambda$-BAP for every finite $\lambda\ge1$.

For each integer $p\ge1$, there are a bounded countably infinite pointed metric space $(M_p,d_p,o)$ and a finite set $A_p\subseteq M_p$ containing $o$ such that $$d_p(x,y)\ge1\quad(x\ne y),\qquad
 \operatorname{diam}M_p\le B_p:=300p^2+150p+5,$$ and every bounded finite-rank linear operator $T_0:\mathcal F(M_p)\to\mathcal F(M_p)$ with $\left\|T_0\right\|\le p$ satisfies $$\max_{a\in A_p}\left\|T_0\delta_a-\delta_a\right\|\ge\frac12.$$

For each integer $p\ge1$, real $\ell_1$ has an equivalent norm $\left\|\cdot\right\|_p$ such that $$\tfrac12\left\|c\right\|_1\le\left\|c\right\|_p\le B_p\left\|c\right\|_1,$$ and $(\ell_1,\left\|\cdot\right\|_p)$ has $2B_p$-BAP but fails $p$-BAP. For $p=1$, this norm fails MAP.

For every even integer $\Delta\ge4$ and positive integer $k$, there is a deterministic sequence of nonempty finite $\Delta$-regular multigraphs $G_m$, with vertices colored by $\{1,\ldots,k\}$, such that, for every fixed integer $r\ge0$ and every possible induced rooted colored radius-$r$ type $\tau$, the fraction of vertices of $G_m$ whose ball has type $\tau$ converges to the probability of $\tau$ for the $\Delta$-regular tree with independent uniform vertex colors.

The preceding construction has the following properties.*

1.  *$(M_p,d_p,o)$ is a countably infinite pointed metric space with separation at least one and diameter at most $B=B_p$. The anchor set $A_p$ is finite and contains $o$. Each source edge has endpoints at $d_p$-distance at most one.*

2.  *The label map $h:M_p\to\{0,\ldots,D\}^k$ is 1-Lipschitz for the sup norm. If a source vertex $x$ has color $i$, then $h_i(x)=0$, and $h(a(x))=h(x)$.*

3.  *For every source vertex $x$ and every anchor $a$, $$d_p(x,a)\ge R=R_p,\qquad d_p(x,a(x))=R.$$ In particular, $d_p(x,o)\ge R_p=30p$.*

4.  *Every closed $d_p$-ball of radius $2L$ has at most $Q$ points. For every $t\in M_p$, at most $H$ coordinates of $h(t)$ are strictly below $D$.

One may enlarge the set counted by $\beta_m$ to include every root whose induced radius-$(n+1)$ neighborhood is not a tree. For fixed $n$, let $\gamma_m$ be the fraction of roots with such a neighborhood and $\widetilde\beta_m$ the enlarged fraction. Then $\beta_m\le\widetilde\beta_m\le\beta_m+\gamma_m$, while the local limit gives $\gamma_m\to0$. Thus [eq:bad-fraction] remains valid with $\widetilde\beta_m$ in place of $\beta_m$, and the same successive choices of $n\ge2$ and sufficiently large $m$ give $\widetilde\beta_m<1/(20V)$.
Let $e:x\to y$ be an incidence of $G$ and let $j,j'\in S$ be states. If $(x,j)$ and $(y,j')$ are compatible and $d_p(j,j')\le2L$, then $j\in E_e$ or $j'\in E_{\bar e}$.

For every incidence $e:x\to y$ of $G$, there is a $1$-Lipschitz function $f_e:M_p\to[-L,L]$ such that $$f_e(j)=b_x(j)\quad(j\in S\setminus E_e),\qquad
 f_e(j')=-b_y(j')\quad(j'\in S\setminus E_{\bar e}).$$

The preceding proof gives the same finite-anchor obstruction for any data satisfying the following assumptions. Fix an integer $p\ge1$ and retain the parameter choices $L,R,K,D,B,V,\Delta,Q,H,k$ of [sec:blocks](#sec:blocks), including [eq:parameters], and the incidence convention of that section. 1. $(N,d,o)$ is a countable pointed metric space of separation at least one and diameter at most $B$, and $A\subseteq N$ is finite and contains $o$. 2. The $G_m$ are nonempty finite $\Delta$-regular multigraphs with disjoint vertex sets in $N$ and colors in $\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Edge endpoints have $d$-distance at most one. For every fixed integer $r\ge0$, the empirical distributions of their induced rooted radius-$r$ colored balls converge to the corresponding distribution on the $\Delta$-regular tree with independent uniform colors, as in [lem:local-limit](#lem:local-limit). 3. The map $h:N\to\{0,\ldots,D\}^k$ is $1$-Lipschitz for the sup norm. Every graph vertex $x$ of color $i$ satisfies $h_i(x)=0$ and has an anchor $a(x)\in A$ with $h(a(x))=h(x)$ and $d(x,a(x))\le R$. 4. Every closed $d$-ball of radius $2L$ has at most $Q$ points, and for every $t\in N$ at most $H$ coordinates of $h(t)$ are strictly below $D$. If these data are fixed before $T_0$, every bounded finite-rank real linear operator $T_0:\mathcal F(N)\to\mathcal F(N)$ with $\left\|T_0\right\|\le p$ satisfies $$\max_{a\in A}\left\|T_0\delta_a-\delta_a\right\|\ge\frac12.$$ Indeed, the support perturbation and signed-measure estimates use only the stated metric, anchor, and label bounds, while the rare-walk, continuation, scalar-test, and averaging steps use only those bounds, the stated graph limit, and the incidence convention.
